title: Túcume pyramids (Huaca Larga)
summary: Túcume, in Lambayeque in northern Peru, is a complex of adobe pyramids (huacas), also called Cerro La Raya. It was an elite urban centre from at least AD 1000 until the Spanish arrived in 1532, used by the Lambayeque, then the Chimú and the Inca. Huaca Larga, 700 m by 280 m and about 30 m high, is probably the most extensive building in the Americas.

uncertainty.note: Mincetur dates the elite urban centre from at least AD 1000 to the Spaniards' arrival in 1532 and also notes abandonment around 1533.

phases.description: Lambayeque builders founded Túcume and its first huacas from about AD 1000.
Chimú builders enlarged Huaca Larga; a Chimú mural dates to about 1375; it was the seat of power under Chimú and Inca occupations.
City abandoned around 1533, soon after the Spanish conquest.

reviewer_note: Model covers Huaca Larga only (700 by 280 by about 30 m, one government inventory; a travel page gives 270 m width and a news page 270 m). Least sure of when Huaca Larga itself was built; the phase dates come from the occupation sequence. Shape mound chosen as closest to a long adobe platform. The huacasdelperu site is a personal site, so the second independent publisher is weak.
